comment: Cross-language golden cases for blob-reference collection. See README.md.

cases.name: prose page HTML img src
cases.why: JP-494: RichTextPage.content is an HTML string, so blob:// is a SUBSTRING, not a standalone value. A walker that only matched whole strings missed every prose blob and the GC swept it.

cases.name: FileShape blobRef raw hash
cases.why: The other of the two reference shapes: a bare hash under a key literally named blobRef.

cases.name: legacy richTextContent Tiptap JSON
cases.why: Legacy prose stored Tiptap JSON, where attrs.src is a standalone string. Must keep working alongside the HTML path.

cases.name: several refs in one string
cases.why: One HTML string may carry many images; the scan must not stop at the first.

cases.name: hex run longer than 64 truncates to 64
cases.why: Both sides take the leading hex run capped at 64 chars, so trailing hex noise still yields a valid hash rather than being rejected.

cases.name: short hash is not a reference
cases.why: Under 64 hex characters is malformed and must be ignored on both sides.

cases.name: uppercase hash is rejected
cases.why: is_valid_blob_hash accepts lowercase only. Pinned because the hex SCAN accepts either case, so the two rules interact and could silently diverge.

cases.name: nested shapes are reached
cases.why: Both walkers recurse the whole body, so a blob inside a grouped/nested shape still counts.

cases.name: blobRef forwarded through an array
cases.why: The relay forwards parent_key into array elements; the client did not. Pinned so the two agree.

cases.name: prose blob and file shape together
cases.why: The end state JP-495 produces: a document holding both reference shapes at once.

cases.name: blobRef carrying the blob:// prefix
cases.why: The blobRef branch validates a BARE hash, so a prefixed value falls to the URI scan instead. Both sides must still yield the bare hash — not the prefixed string as an id.

cases.name: a non-hash blobRef is not a reference
cases.why: Blob ids are SHA-256 hex (BlobStorage.computeHash), so a value that isn't one cannot name a stored blob. Collecting it would put an id in the set that no blob can ever match.

cases.name: an empty blobRef is not a reference
cases.why: A freshly created FileShape carries blobRef: '' before its upload completes.

cases.name: a whole-string blob:// with a malformed tail is ignored
cases.why: Same reasoning as the non-hash blobRef: the tail cannot name a stored blob. Pinned because the obvious implementation special-cases a string that STARTS WITH the prefix and would collect the junk tail.

cases.name: no references
cases.why: An empty document derives an empty set, not a crash.
